content.comment_body: I have set up a customized website with a home page and an additional page. The navigation menu is linked correctly in the web server software. When accessing the site using Google Chrome, the home page appears, but the navigation bar is missing, preventing me from accessing the other page. In Firefox, the sidebar appears, and in Windows Edge, the sidebar is both visible and functional. I updated Google Chrome to the latest version and enabled JavaScript, but the issue persists. Has anyone else encountered this and found a solution? Thank you.
You might try forcing a page reload using Ctrl + Shift + R.

Force refreshing did not help. I reinstalled the web editor software, formatted the SD card, and reloaded the website project. Only Edge browser shows the Page Navigation Menu properly. In Chrome and Firefox, I can only access the home screen.
I have not encountered this issue with Google Chrome Version 97.0.4692.99 (64-bit).

Thanks for checking; I am using the same Chrome build. It seems there may be a setting or something else I am missing. Interestingly, it used to work in Chrome before. Since Microsoft Edge uses the Chromium engine, I would expect it to have the same issue if the problem was browser-related. Could this be related to port forwarding or the requirement for it? Apologies for the repeat post; the page reset during submission, so I posted twice by mistake.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing inconsistent display and operation of the navigation sidebar in their website project across different browsers. The sidebar functions properly in Microsoft Edge but is either hidden or not working in Chrome and Firefox for some. Troubleshooting steps such as browser updates, enabling JavaScript, and reinstalling relevant software have not resolved the issue. There is uncertainty about the cause, with some users speculating about browser settings or network configurations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the navigation sidebar of their website to be accessible and function consistently across all major web browsers to facilitate navigation to different pages.
